## Finding from the 2026-04-22 full-flywheel dogfood on #26 (PR #57)

`SymphonyElixir.Verification.maybe_critique/2` at `elixir/lib/symphony_elixir/verification.ex:107` returns `:approve` **silently**. Only the reject, timeout, and codex-failure paths emit log lines:

- `elixir/lib/symphony_elixir/verification.ex:114` ΓÇö `warning: Verification critic failed (fail-open): ...`
- `elixir/lib/symphony_elixir/verification.ex:119` ΓÇö `warning: Verification critic timed out (fail-open)`
- `elixir/lib/symphony_elixir/orchestrator.ex` ΓÇö `info: Critic rejected recipe for ...`

## Why it matters

In the #26 dogfood, verification passed in 13s and the dogfood log showed **zero critic-related entries**. From the logs alone it was impossible to tell whether the critic actually fired, fail-opened silently (shouldn't ΓÇö that path logs), or was bypassed. I had to boot iex and re-parse the workflow YAML to confirm `critic_enabled: true` was in effect.

Claimed value of the critic gate (#42) was breaking the correlated-error blind spot. If we can't see it running on healthy approvals, we can't tell when it silently regresses.

## Proposal

Emit an info-level log on every critic invocation outcome, including approvals. Minimal shape:

```
info: Verification critic approved for issue_id=... identifier=...
info: Verification critic rejected for issue_id=... identifier=... reason=...
```

Optionally include `codex_seconds` and a short reason snippet in structured fields once metrics are a priority. The approve log is the load-bearing piece ΓÇö rejection/timeout/fail already log.

## Acceptance

- Every codepath through `maybe_critique/2` emits at least one log line carrying the verdict.
- A passing critic run in a dogfood is visibly distinguishable from a run where the critic was disabled.
title: feat(verification): log critic outcomes on approve (observability gap)

body:
## Problem

The `check-integration` command has a name that strongly implies a system-health / doctor command (validate token, gh auth, bundle, state, scout dependency, Gist reachability). In reality, it is a feature-branch helper that runs `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=A <base>...HEAD` plus `git grep` to find orphan new files on the current branch. It performs zero system diagnostics.

There is no real `doctor` / `self-test` / `check-setup` command in the CLI. `checkSetup` in the registry only reads `config.setupComplete` ΓÇö a single boolean ΓÇö which is not useful when users hit the common failure modes (missing token, missing bundle, corrupted state, unreachable scout).

## Evidence

- `packages/core/src/commands/check-integration.ts` ΓÇö module docstring at line 3: *"Detects new files in the current branch that aren't referenced elsewhere."*
- JSON shape: `{newFiles: NewFileInfo[], unreferencedCount: number}` where `NewFileInfo = {path, referencedBy: string[], isIntegrated: boolean, suggestedEntryPoints?: string[]}`.
- Implementation runs `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=A <base>...HEAD` and `git grep -l -- <pattern>`. No token check, no bundle check, no gh CLI check, no `GET /user` ping, no state.json parse check, no scout resolution check.
- `cli-registry.ts` ΓÇö the `check-setup` registry entry only inspects `config.setupComplete`, a boolean.
- When `git ls-files` fails (not a git repo), `allFiles = []` silently, so every file becomes `isIntegrated: false` ΓÇö confusing output with no loud error.

## Proposed fix

**Two parts:**

### 1. Rename the existing command

Rename `check-integration` to something that describes what it does, e.g. `orphan-files`, `new-file-audit`, or `branch-integration`. Keep the existing behavior; only the name changes. Update `cli-registry.ts`, test filenames, any references in workflows/agents, and the help text.

### 2. Add a real `doctor` command

Create `packages/core/src/commands/doctor.ts` exporting `runDoctor()` that produces a `DoctorOutput` envelope:

```ts
interface DoctorOutput {
  checks: Array<{
    name: string;
    status: 'ok' | 'warning' | 'error';
    message: string;
    remediation?: string;
  }>;
  summary: { ok: number; warnings: number; errors: number };
}
```

Checks to include:
- `$GITHUB_TOKEN` or `gh auth token` resolves (hit `GET /user`, parse login).
- `gh` CLI present and authenticated (`gh auth status`).
- `packages/core/dist/cli.bundle.cjs` exists and mtime is newer than `packages/core/src/cli.ts`.
- `~/.oss-autopilot/state.json` parses and `schemaVersion === current`.
- `@oss-scout/core` resolvable (`require.resolve`).
- GitHub Search API rate-limit status (`GET /rate_limit`).
- If Gist mode: gist reachable and writable.

Wire into `cli-registry.ts` as `doctor` (needs auth for the live API ping; flag gracefully when no token so the other checks still run).

Optional: surface from the plugin `/oss` menu as "Run diagnostic."

## Acceptance criteria

- `check-integration` is renamed; the existing feature-branch behavior is preserved under the new name.
- `oss-autopilot doctor --json` returns a structured checks array.
- Every check emits `ok`/`warning`/`error` with an actionable `remediation` string on failure.
- The command works even when `$GITHUB_TOKEN` is missing (skips the GitHub API checks with a clear `warning`).
- Unit tests mock each external dependency (fs for bundle, `require.resolve` for scout, Octokit for API) and cover the ok + error paths.
- `workflows/reference.md` documents the new `doctor` command.

## Scope / out-of-scope

**In scope:** rename + new `doctor` command + tests + reference.md update.

**Out of scope:** auto-repair (e.g. running the rebuild automatically); that belongs in a future follow-up.

**Severity:** High ┬╖ **Area:** CLI diagnostics ┬╖ **Audit ref:** H4

labels.name: priority:high
labels.description: High priority - should be addressed soon
